GROUND RULES: ALL CONTESTANTS - The "30-hour replacement" policy and the "walk-up replacement" policy will be in effect. See Rodeo Entry Information page of the business journal. NOTE: Money won at this event in SB will count towards 2026 X-Broncs standings. Money won at this event will count towards qualifications for the 2026 National Finals Rodeo and the 2026 Rookie of the Year Standings, as long as the contestant has entered and competed in a minimum of forty (40) PRCA rodeos during the 2026 rodeo year. Money won will not count for circuit standings or All Around standings. This event will not be applied to the contestants required circuit participation count. EF's: $100 EF plus $35 Central Entry Office/Supplemental Insurance Fee.
STK CONT.: Various

GROUND RULES: Contestants who choose to enter the Legacy Steer Roping event must be at least 50 years old or a permit holder at the time of entry closing. They must also be entered in the steer roping event at the Steer Roping Event in Lovington. To be eligible, the contestant must not have been an NFSR qualifier during the past three years. Contestants will pay entry fees of $400. Contestants will not compete on any additional steers. The times that are recorded for the contestants' competition runs at the Steer Roping Event in Lovington will be used to determine the pay-off. There will be no additional added money and since no additional animals will be run, there will be no additional stock charge or PROCOM charge.

Money won in the Legacy Steer Roping will not count towards PRCA World Standings, circuit standings, All Around standings, or for money won qualifications. It will count towards qualifying for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals held in conjunction with the National Finals Steer Roping. (NFSR qualifiers will not be eligible for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals).
STK CONT.: Various

detailLines: San Angelo TX NPP
April 18
San Angelo Cinch Chute-Out
ARENA: San Angelo Coliseum
ADDRESS: 50 E. 43rd St
PERFS: 1 Perf: April 18- 7:00 PM
EVENTS: BB SB BR TD SW @ $10000 TR-HD, TR-HL @ $10000
SPECIAL ENTRY FEES: BB-$250; SB-$250; BR-$250; TD-$250; SW-$250; TR-$250
PERMITS: BB SB BR TD SW TR
FINALS: April 18- 7:00 PM BB SB BR TD SW TR

GROUND RULES: ALL EVENTS - The "30-hour replacement" and "walk-up replacement" policies will be in effect. See Rodeo Information page of the business journal. PROCOM and the rodeo secretary will work together finding replacements for contestants who turn out after the 30-hour deadline.
ALL EVENTS - Re-entries will be accepted for available positions on Fri., April 10 between 9am -11am. See Rodeo Entry Information Page of the business journal.
GRACE PERIOD - Will expire one hour after entries close.

FORMAT - One go-round with a top 3 chute out round during the same performance. Any ties for the top 3 positions will be broken by random draw by the judges. If there are less than three qualified times or scores in an event, a random draw by the judges will determine who advances to fill the remaining positions in the chute out (not to exceed three).

QUALIFICATIONS: ALL EVENTS - 10 entries. All from 2026 money won. No exemptions. In the TR, the 10 headers that qualify must rope with the 10 heelers that qualify. If a contestants partner is drawn out due to qualification, the contestant who qualified will not be allowed to draw out. A replacement partner will be drawn at random from the other contestants whose partners were drawn out due to qualifications. If a header or heeler T.O.'s or D,R.'s prior to the 30-hour deadline, leaving an incomplete team, the next contestant in the corresponding category (header or heeler) on the alternate list will be added. If a notification is not made prior to the 30-hour deadline, the remaining partner may select another partner from among any of the PRCA event contestants already entered at the rodeo, except those scheduled to compete in the TR.

PAY-OFF FOR THE FINALS: $7,500 for first, $3,000 for second, and $2,000 for third. Total of $12,500. If there are not 3 qualified scores or times in the Chute Out Round, the remaining placings will be paid based on highest scores or fastest times from the long go-round. There will be no pay-out for the long go-round or the average. Only money paid out to a contestant without a qualified score or time in either go-round will be considered ground money. All other money paid out will count for PRCA World Standings, but will not count for circuit standings. This event will not count towards the required circuit participation count.
NOTE: The 6% of the purse that is collected by the PRCA will not be held out of the total purse. It will be paid directly to the PRCA by the San Angelo committee.
STK CONT.: Pete Carr Pro Rodeo

They must also be entered in the steer roping event at the Guymon Pioneer Days Rodeo. To be eligible, the contestant must not have been an NFSR qualifier during the past 3 years. Contestants will pay entry fees of $400. Contestants will not compete on any additional steers. Only the four go-rounds and the average after four go-rounds will be included in the pay-off for the Legacy Steer Roping. There will be no additional added money and since no additional animals will be run, there will be no additional stock charge or PROCOM charge.

Money won in the Legacy Steer Roping will not count towards PRCA World Standings, circuit standings, All Around standings, or for money won qualifications. It will count towards qualifying for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals held in conjunction with the National Finals Steer Roping. (NFSR qualifiers will not be eligible for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals).

PERFS: 1 Perf: May 9- 6:00 PM
EVENTS: SB @ $22500
SPECIAL ENTRY FEES: SB-$150
PERMITS: SB
GROUND RULES: ALL CONTESTANTS - May also enter online at www.rodeocanada.com between April 20 at 8 AM and April 21 at 2 PM.

Re-entries: Re-entries will be accepted where the actual entries accepted during the original entry period were less than the limit. Entries re-opened sometime prior to the riding event stock draw. Contestants that enter during the re-entry period will be placed in the remaining available positions (available positions will be defined by the stock contractor and/or committee based on the number of contestants that entered during the re-entry period). All re-entries will be accepted to fill the performances not to exceed the original limit defined in the ground rules (based on "money won" qualifications).
Standardized Alternate Replacement Procedure will be in place for this event based on CPRA 2026 Rulebook (standardized ground rules)

If a contestant notifies a turn-out, DR or visible release and is replaced by an alternate, the alternate contestant will be responsible for the entry fees. If the contestant that notified the turnout or visible release is not replaced by an alternate, they will be responsible for the entry fee. If a contestant properly doctor releases they will not be responsible for entry fees.
Walk up Replacement (implemented for 2026 season) will be in place for this event based on CPRA 2026 Rulebook (standardized ground rules).

If a contestant notifies a turn out, DR, or visible release and is replaced by an alternate at a limited entry event, the alternate contestant will be responsible for the entry fees. If a contestant properly doctor releases they will not be responsible for entry fees. Also, if a contestant turns out and is not replaced, they will be responsible for entry fees and he will receive a $250 fine (does not include DR's and VR's).
Qualifications: Maximum 30 contestants.
top 100 blended CPRA/PRCA from the 2025 standings and the 2026 standings as of April 17th 2026, will be used to determine draw outs.

Remaining positions, if any of the qualification categories are not filled by contestants with dollars won, will be filled by first the final 2025 CPRA standings, the 2025 PRCA standings, then a random draw of card holders, then semi-pro card holders. If there are still open positions, all remaining openings will be filled by a random draw of permit holders.
Format:
One Go round with Top eight (8) advancing to finals.

Top eight (8) will then pick their own finals stock out of a pen of twelve (12). First (1st) place coming into the finals getting first pick down to eighth (8th). The remaining four (4) horses will be the finals re-rides (randomly drawn order). If there are not eight (8) qualified rides during the long go, all remaining positions will be filled by random draw. If the 8th place is tied going into the finals, the tie will be broken by highest marked spur ride from the long go, if still tied, spots will be determined by random draw by the judges.
Contestants who did not have a qualified score in the first go-round and are drawn back to compete in the finals, will not be eligible to place in the aggregate.
PAYOUT: One go-round with a (top 8) finals. $5,000 held out for short go, 6 places paid in long go, 6 places paid in aggregate, 4 places paid in short go.
Contestant Info: Only cards accepted at gate will be contestants entered and 1 companion. All others must pay at the gate. No exceptions.
ENTRY FEES: SB - $90. CRES, circuit, & other associate fees with be charged in addition to all entry fees as per the rule book.

TURN OUT/ALTERNATE PROCEDURE: Contestants who have originally entered and were eligible at time of entry but were drawn out will be added to an alternate list. These contestants will be notified of any turn-outs or doctor releases and be given the option of re-entry up to 24 hours prior to rodeo turn out deadline, any turnouts done after the alternate time frame will be filled by walk up replacements only. If stock has already been drawn in the rough stock they will draw stock from a pool of animals consisting of all turned out stock for that performance and all re-ride stock for that performance.

NOTE: In order for money won in the Lakeland Xtreme Broncs in Cold Lake, AB to count for qualification for the 2026 National Finals Rodeo or the 2026 Rookie of the Year standings, a contestant must have entered and competed at a minimum of 40 PRCA rodeos during the 2026 season. Money won at Lakeland will not count towards All Around. Money won will also count towards X-Broncs standings.
STK CONT.: Various

Standardized Alternate Replacement Procedure will be in place for this event based on CPRA 2026 Rulebook (standardized ground rules) If a contestant notifies a turn-out, DR or visible release and is replaced by an alternate, the alternate contestant will be responsible for the entry fees. If the contestant that notified the turnout or visible release is not replaced by an alternate, they will be responsible for the entry fee. If a contestant properly doctor releases they will not be responsible for entry fees. Walk up Replacement (implemented for 2026 season) will be in place for this event based on CPRA 2026 Rulebook (standardized ground rules). If a contestant notifies a turn out, DR, or visible release and is replaced by an alternate at a limited entry event, the alternate contestant will be responsible for the entry fees. If a contestant properly doctor releases they will not be responsible for entry fees. Remaining positions, if any of the qualification categories are not filled by contestants with dollars won, will be filled by first the final 2025 CPRA standings, the 2025 PRCA standings, then a random draw of card holders, then semi-pro card holders. If there are still open positions, all remaining openings will be filled by a random draw of permit holders. Format: One Go round with Top eight (8) advancing to finals. Top eight (8) will then pick their own finals stock out of a pen of twelve (12). First (1st) place coming into the finals getting first pick down to eighth (8th). The remaining four (4) horses will be the finals re-rides (randomly drawn order). If there are not eight (8) qualified rides during the long go, all remaining positions will be filled by random draw. If the 8th place is tied going into the finals, the tie will be broken by highest marked spur ride from the long go, if still tied, spots will be determined by random draw by the judges. Contestants who did not have a qualified score in the first go-round and are drawn back to compete in the finals, will not be eligible to place in the aggregate.PAYOUT: One go-round with a (top 8) finals. $5,000 held out for short go, 6 places paid in long go, 6 places paid in aggregate, 4 places paid in short go.Contestant Info: Only cards accepted at gate will be contestants entered and 1 companion. All others must pay at the gate. No exceptions.ENTRY FEES: SB - $90. CRES, circuit, & other associate fees with be charged in addition to all entry fees as per the rule book.TURN OUT/ALTERNATE PROCEDURE: Contestants who have originally entered and were eligible at time of entry but were drawn out will be added to an alternate list. These contestants will be notified of any turn-outs or doctor releases and be given the option of re-entry up to 24 hours prior to rodeo turn out deadline, any turnouts done after the alternate time frame will be filled by walk up replacements only. If stock has already been drawn in the rough stock they will draw stock from a pool of animals consisting of all turned out stock for that performance and all re-ride stock for that performance.NOTE: In order for money won in the Lakeland Xtreme Broncs in Cold Lake, AB to count for qualification for the 2026 National Finals Rodeo or the 2026 Rookie of the Year standings, a contestant must have entered and competed at a minimum of 40 PRCA rodeos during the 2026 season. SPECIAL ENTRY FEES: SB-$150
PERMITS: SB
GROUND RULES: ALL CONTESTANTS - May also enter online at www.rodeocanada.com between May 13 at 8 AM and May 14 at 2 PM.
All Contestants: Re-entries, if needed, will be accepted for available positions 48 hours after entries close from 8am-2pm. See Rodeo Entry Information on Rodeo Schedule.

QUALIFICATIONS: Maximum 30 contestants based on top 100 blended CPRA/PRCA standing as of Monday 13,2024 will be used to determine draw outs. If the qualifications are not filled by contestants with dollars won leaving open positions; the remaining openings will be filled by a random draw of card holders then semi-pro card holders. If there are still open positions, all remaining openings will be filled by a random draw of permit holders.

FORMAT: One go-round with a Top eight (8) will advance to finals. If there are not eight (8) qualified rides during the long go, all remaining positions will be filled by random draw. If the 8th place is tied going into the finals, the tie will be broken by highest marked spur ride from the long go, if still tied spots will be determined by random draw.
PAYOUT: 50% of the total purse for the long go and 50% for the short go. Long Go will pay 8 places and Short Go will pay 4 places - 40%, 30%, 20%, 10%. There will be no average payout.

TURN OUT/ALTERNATE PROCEDURE: Contestants who have originally entered and were eligible at time of entry but were drawn out will be added to an alternate list. These contestants will be notified of any turn-outs or doctor releases and be given the option of re-entry up to 24 hours prior to rodeo turn out deadline, any turnouts done after the alternate time frame will be filled by walk up replacements only. If stock has already been drawn in the rough stock they will draw stock from a pool of animals consisting of all turned out stock for that performance.

Walk Up Replacements: Contestants who have originally entered and were eligible at time of entry but were drawn out may, in person, check with the rodeo secretary no later than 1 hour prior to the performance to confirm their availability and desire to be an alternate. If selected, by random draw of all walk ups available, an alternate will assume the competition position of the contestant that he is replacing, in the rough stock they will draw stock from a pool of animals consisting of all turned out stock for that performance.

Re-entries: Re-entries will be accepted where the actual entries accepted during the original entry period were less than the limit. Entries be re-opened sometime prior to the riding event stock draw. Contestants that enter during the re-entry period will be placed in the remaining available positions (available positions will be defined by the stock contractor and/or committee based on the number of contestants that entered during the re-entry period). All re-entries will be accepted to fill the performances not to exceed the original limit defined in the ground rules (based on "money won" qualifications).

If a contestant notifies a turn-out, DR or visible release and is replaced by an alternate, the alternate contestant will be responsible for the entry fees. If the contestant that notified the turnout or visible release is not replaced by an alternate, they will be responsible for the entry fee. If a contestant properly doctor releases they will not be responsible for entry fees.
Entry Fees: SB: $150
+CRES & other associate fees with be charged in addition to all entry fees as per the rule book.

NOTE: Money won at this event will count towards the Xbroncs Standings. Money won at this event will count towards qualification for the 2026 National finals Rodeo and the 2026 Rookie of the Year Standings as long as the contestant competed at a minimum of 40 PRCA rodeos during the 2026 Rodeo year. Money won at this event will not count towards All Around Standings.
STK CONT.: Outlawbuckers Rodeo

The top 10 from the Qualifying Performance on June 6 will advance to the Darby Extreme Bareback event on June 7.

If ties result in more than 10 to advance (will not exceed 10), the tied contestant with the single highest score in either go-round will advance. If still tied, the tied contestant with the highest ranking in 2026 World Standings (as of 7 days prior to entry closing) will advance. If a contestant does not accept advancement to the Extreme event due to injury or any other reason, the contestant with the next highest ranking in the average from the Qualifier will advance.

NOTE: This event will count for qualification for the 2026 National Finals Rodeo and the 2026 Rookie of the Year Standings as long as the contestant has competed at a minimum of 40 PRCA rodeos during the 2026 rodeo year. Money won at this event will not count towards All Around or Circuit Standings nor will the event be applied to a contestant's required circuit participation count.

detailLines: Darby MT NPP
June 7
Dutton Ranch Darby Xtreme Bareback
ARENA: Richard Cromwell Arena
ADDRESS: 200 Rodeo Rd,
PERFS: 1 Perf: June 7- 3:00 PM
EVENTS: BB @ $50000
SPECIAL ENTRY FEES: BB-$250
PERMITS: BB

GROUND RULES: ALL CONTESTANTS - Contestants who turn-out or doctor's release the Darby Extreme Bareback event on June 7 will be replaced by the next highest ranking on the alternate list for the Extreme event which will be based on highest scores in the average from the Qualifying Performance on June 6.
GRACE PERIOD: Will expire one hour after entries close.

QUALIFICATIONS: 30 entries will be accepted for the Darby Extreme Bareback event on Sun., June 7. The top 20 who enter based on 2026 PRCA World Standings (as of 7 days prior to entry closing) will be accepted as entries for the Darby Extreme Bareback event on Sunday, June 7. Ten contestants will advance from the Qualifying Performance on Saturday, June 6 to the Extreme event on Sunday, June 7. If less than 20 contestants enter the Darby Extreme Bareback event on June 7, remaining available positions will be filled from contestants advancing from the Qualifying performance based on highest scores (not to exceed a total of 30).

FORMAT FOR THE QUALIFYING PERFORMANCE: The Qualifying Performance will be either one go-round, two go-rounds, or one go-round with progressive round depending on the number of entries. If one go-round, the contestants with ten highest scores in the Qualifying Performance will advance to the Extreme Event (will not exceed ten). If ties result in more than ten to advance, the tied contestant(s) with the highest ranking in the 2026 World Standings (as of 7 days prior to entry closing) will advance. If two go-rounds or one go-round with a progressive round or a finals, the ten contestants with the highest rankings in the average after two go-rounds will advance to Extreme event. If ties result in more than ten to advance, the tied contestant with the single highest score in the Qualifying Performance will advance. If a contestant does not accept advancement to the Extreme event due to injury in the Qualifying performance or any other reason, the contestant with the next highest ranking in the average from the Qualifying performance will advance. Ten contestants will advance.

FORMAT FOR THE EXTREME EVENT: One go-round with a top 12 finals. The 30 contestants will be placed into 3 sections with 10 contestants in each section. Contestants, who enter, based on their rankings in the 2026 World Standings (as of 7 days prior to entry closing) will be placed in the section as follows: Section one: 1, 6, 7, 12, 13, 18, 19 and 1st, 4th, and 9th from the Qualifying Performance. Section two: 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, and 2nd, 5th, and 8th from the Qualifying Performance. Section three: 3, 4, 9, 10, 15, 16, and 3rd, 6th, 7th, and 10th from the Qualifying Performance. Contestants ranking will be dependent on the contestants who enter. For example, if the contestant who is ranked 1st in the standings does not enter, and the contestant who is ranked 2nd does enter, the contestant who is ranked 2nd in the standings will fill the #1 position since he was the highest ranked contestant who actually entered. After the contestants have been placed in the three sections, PROCOM will draw a random order for the contestants within each section to be listed on the judges sheets. The top 4 contestants based on highest scores from each of the three sections will advance to the finals. If ties result in more than 4 to advance, see following tie breaker procedure. If there are less than 4 qualified rides in a section, the contestant with the next highest score from the other sections who is not already advancing, will advance to fill that position.

TIE BREAKER PROCEDURE - Prior to the event, the judges will randomly draw a number (1 through 30) for each of the 30 contestants. This number will be used to break any ties for advancement to the finals. For example, if 4th place in a section is tied between two contestants, and one contestant's drawn number is #1 and the other contestant's drawn number is #12, the contestant with the lowest number which in the example is #1, will advance to the finals.

TURN-OUT, DR's and VIR's in the Darby Extreme Bareback event on Sunday will be replaced by contestants from the alternate list. If the Qualifying Performance is one go-round, the order of the alternate list will be based on highest single scores in the Qualifying Performance. If the Qualifying Performance is two go-rounds or one go-round with a progressive or a finals, the alternate list will be based on highest rankings in the average. Contestants who desire to be used as alternates must check-in with the rodeo secretary no later than one hour prior to the start of the Extreme event. After the one hour check-in deadline, the alternates will be randomly drawn to the available positions. If stock has already been drawn the alternate contestant will compete on the animal that has been drawn by the contestant that he is replacing.
DRAFT PROCESS - Will be used to assign stock to contestants. The draft process will occur at the rodeo secretary's office (or location still to be determined) 2 hours prior to the start of the event.

STOCK DRAW FOR THREE SECTIONS: There will be 12 horses set for each section with 10 contestants in each section. In order listed on the judges sheets, each contestant will draw a number, 1 through 10. The contestant who draws #1 will be the first to select an animal on which he will compete. Contestants will select their competition animals in order of the numbers that they draw. If a contestant is not physically present to select his animal, he will be moved to the bottom of the draw order. After all contestants who are present has selected their competition animals, the judges will draw animals for the contestants who are not present from the remaining animals not yet selected. The two animals not selected will become the re-rides. A coin flip will determine which will be the first re-ride. This procedure will be followed for all three sections. The time and location of the draft process will be included in PROCOM callbacks.

STOCK DRAW FOR THE FINALS: The buck order of the horses to be used in the finals will be established prior to the stock draw. The draw order will be based on scores in the long go-round. The contestant with the highest score in the long go-round will draw first and the contestant with the lowest score in the long go-round will draw last. If there are ties in the placings advancing to the finals, the tie breaker procedure will be used to determine the order in which the tied contestants draw. The competition order will be based on pre-established buck order of the horses.

ENTRY FEES: Entry fees for the 20 contestants who are originally accepted as entries for the Darby Extreme Bareback event on June 7 will be $250 (plus $35 supplemental fee).Entry fees for contestants accepted as entries for the Qualifying Performance will be $100 (plus $35 supplemental fee). The $100 entry fees for the Qualifying performance will be included in the pay-off for the Qualifying performance. The contestants who advance from the Qualifying Performance to the Darby Extreme Bareback event will not be required to pay any additional fees.

PAY-OFF for the DARBY EXTREME BAREBACK EVENT on Sun., June 7: $50,000 added plus $5,000 in entry fees for 20 contestants minus $3,300 for the 6% equals $51,700 to be included in the pay-off. $5,000 will be allotted to each of the three sections ($15,000 total), each section will pay $2,000 for 1st; $1,500 for 2nd; $1,000 for 3rd; and $500 for 4th. The remaining $36,700 will be paid out for the finals (the amount allotted for the finals may vary slightly due to doctor's released contestants who are not replaced. There will be no average pay-off. The finals will pay 6 places. The percentages paid for the 6 places will be in accordance with the Rulebook (R5.4.1).

NOTE: This event will count for qualification for the 2026 National Finals Rodeo and the 2026 Rookie of the Year Standings as long as the contestant has competed at a minimum of 40 PRCA rodeos during the 2026 rodeo year. Money won at this event will not count towards All Around or Circuit Standings nor will the event be applied to a contestant's required circuit participation count.
STK CONT.: Various
SUB. CONT.: Pickett Pro Rodeo Co. , J Bar J, Legacy Pro Rodeo LLC

(NFSR qualifiers will not be eligible for the Legacy Steer Roping Finals).

In the rough stock, they will draw stock from a pool of animals consisting of all turned-out stock for the performance and all re-ride stock for that performance.

GROUND RULES: Only actual contestant and one companion allowed gate access. Companions may receive their ticket at the secretary's office. All trailers must enter at Gate B. Check-in at Ford Idaho Center Horse Park office for stalls and parking.
ALL EVENTS - The "30-hour replacement" policy will be in effect. See Rodeo Entry Information Section of the Business Journal.
ALL EVENTS - The "walk-up replacement" policy will be in effect. See Rodeo Entry Information Section of the Business Journal.
ALL EVENTS - Re-entries will be accepted for available positions on Mon., June 8 between 9 AM and 11 AM. See Rodeo Entry Information section of the business journal.
RIDING EVENT TRADE DEADLINE - Fri., June 5 at 4 PM. All confirmed trades will be final and will be processed immediately after both involved parties have confirmed through PROCOM.

TIMED EVENT TRADE DEADLINE - Wed., June 10 at 4 PM. All confirmed trades will be final and will be processed immediately after both involved parties have confirmed through PROCOM. Contestants who are placed in the performances will be allowed to trade their second go-round positions with contestants who are placed in other performances. Contestants will not be allowed to trade from a performance to the slack. The rodeo secretary will post the trade deadline in the rodeo office.
TE - If a timed event animal escapes or a re-run is awarded for any other reason during a performance, the extra will be used. Only escaped animals go back into herd.
TR - Only two loops allowed.

TD, SW, TR FORMAT - Two go-rounds plus a top 12 finals. All contestants will run their first go-round in the slack. The top 50 based on fastest times from the first go-round will be placed in the first 5 performances and the remaining contestants will run their second go-round in reverse order of the first go-round in slack, following the completion of the first go-round. If there are less than 50 qualified times in the first go-round, the remaining available positions in the performances (not to exceed 50) will be filled by the contestants with no qualified times in the first go-round based on the placement order for the second go-round. If ties result in more than 50 to be placed in the performances, a random draw will determine which of the tied contestants will be placed in the performances (will not exceed 50). Placement in the performances will be in accordance with R2.6 of the PRCA Rulebook (pertaining to progressive go-rounds). Contestants who are placed in the performances will not be allowed to trade to the slack. Contestants will be allowed to trade from one performance to a different performance, up to 5 PM the day prior to the 1st performance.

ALL EVENTS - If a contestant who qualifies for the Finals notifies a turn-out, doctors release, or a visible injury release through PROCOM, the constant with the next highest ranking in the average may be contacted by Procom and placed in that available position. Non-notified turn-outs and visible injury releases after the turn-out deadline will not be replaced. If the next highest ranked contestant is not available to accept the position the next highest ranked contestant may be contacted and placed in that position. This procedure will be followed until all positions are filled. The replacement contestant's competition order will be based on his ranking in the average (not on the ranking of the contestant that he is replacing). In riding events, if an animal has already been drawn for a contestant who has turned-out, the replacement contestant will draw an animal from a pool consisting of all animals that have been turned-out (includes DR's and VIR's).
GB - Approved for first slack event in accordance with R4.9.4.

SLACK ORDER - Sunday, June 14 at 7:00 AM: GB (1st go-round), Breakaway (1st Go-round), TD (1st go-round with the exception of approximately 30 contestants that will compete during Monday's slack), Breakaway (2nd go-round), SW (approximately 50% of the 1st go-round. Monday, June 15 at 7:00 AM: TR (1st go-round), TD (finish 1st go-round with about 30 contestants), SW (finish the second half of the 1st go-round), TD (2nd go-round), GB (2nd go-round). Tuesday, June 16 at 8:30 AM: TR (2nd go-round), SW (2nd go-round).
QUALIFICATIONS: BB - 60 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack. W/F's (12) $5,000 held out for finals.
SB - 70 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack. W/F's (12) $5,000 held out for finals.
BR - 80 minimum entries. No compensation. No slack. W/F's (12) $5,000 held out for finals. There may be two sections.
TD, SW, TR - 110 minimum entries.
STK CONT.: Cervi Championship Rodeo

ALL EVENTS - Re-entries will be accepted for available positions at a time set by the CPRA after entries close to coincide with other entry schedules (typically all events for a particular weekend that require re-entries will be held on the same day) from 10am-12pm. ALL EVENTS - Walk up Replacement (implemented for 2026 season ) will be in place for this event based on CPRA 2026 Rulebook (standardized ground rules)

ALL CONTESTANTS - If a contestant notifies a turn out, DR, or visible release and is replaced by an alternate at a limited entry event, the alternate contestant will be responsible for the entry fees. If a contestant properly doctor releases they will not be responsible for entry fees. Also, if a contestant turns out and is not replaced, they will be responsible for entry fees and he will receive a $250 fine (does not include DR's and VR's).
